readme:
# Google Play Scraper

Search [Google Play](https://play.google.com) apps by keyword, or look up apps by package name or app page URL. You get one record per app: title, developer with the contact details shown on the listing, rating and rating histogram, install band, price, in-app purchase and ads flags, content rating, release and update dates, description, screenshots and similar apps. Use it for app store research, competitor tracking, and lists of app publishers by niche with their public support email, website and address.

## What you get

One record per app. Fields that an app or a record type does not have are `null` (or an empty list).

There are two record types, shown in `record_type`:

- `detail`: the full record. Every field in the table below.
- `search`: only what the search list shows (the fields marked "search" below). Keyword results are returned as `detail` records by default (`includeDetails` on); a `search` record appears when you switch that option off, or as a fallback when an app's page could not be read.

| Field | Type | Records | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `record_type` | string | both | `detail` or `search` |
| `app_id` | string | both | Package name, for example `com.duolingo` |
| `title` | string | both | App title |
| `url` | string | both | Public app page |
| `summary` | string or null | detail | Short description |
| `developer` | string or null | both | Developer name |
| `developer_id` | string or null | detail | Developer ID |
| `developer_url` | string or null | detail | Developer page on Google Play |
| `developer_email` | string or null | detail | Support email shown on the listing |
| `developer_website` | string or null | detail | Developer website shown on the listing |
| `developer_address` | string or null | detail | Postal address shown on the listing |
| `developer_phone` | string or null | detail | Phone number shown on the listing, when given |
| `privacy_policy_url` | string or null | detail | Privacy policy link |
| `category` | string or null | both | Category name in the chosen language |
| `genre_id` | string or null | detail | Category ID, language independent, for example `EDUCATION` |
| `score` | number or null | both | Average rating, 1 to 5. `null` for apps without ratings |
| `ratings_count` | integer or null | detail | Number of ratings |
| `reviews_count` | integer or null | detail | Number of written reviews |
| `histogram` | object or null | detail | Ratings per star, keys `1` to `5` |
| `installs` | string or null | both | Install band as shown, for example `500,000,000+` |
| `installs_min` | integer or null | detail | Lower end of the install band |
| `installs_max` | integer or null | detail | Upper end of the band. Derived: the start of the next band minus one |
| `price` | number or null | both | Price in the store currency, `0` for free apps |
| `currency` | string or null | both | Currency code of the price |
| `free` | boolean or null | both | True when the price is 0 |
| `offers_iap` | boolean or null | detail | True when the app has in-app purchases |
| `iap_price_range` | string or null | detail | In-app purchase price range as shown on the listing |
| `contains_ads` | boolean or null | detail | True when the listing says the app contains ads |
| `content_rating` | string or null | both | Content rating label in the chosen language |
| `content_rating_descriptors` | string or null | detail | Content rating descriptors |
| `released` | string or null | detail | First release time (ISO 8601, UTC) |
| `released_text` | string or null | detail | First release date as shown in the chosen language |
| `updated` | string or null | detail | Last update time (ISO 8601, UTC) |
| `updated_text` | string or null | detail | Last update date as shown in the chosen language |
| `version` | string or null | detail | Always `null`: the app version is not on the listing page |
| `android_version` | string or null | detail | Always `null`: the minimum Android version is not on the listing page |
| `description` | string or null | both | Full description as plain text (search records: the short text of the search list) |
| `recent_changes` | string or null | detail | What's new text |
| `icon` | string or null | both | App icon |
| `header_image` | string or null | detail | Feature graphic |
| `screenshots` | array | both | Screenshot URLs |
| `video` | string or null | detail | Trailer URL when the listing has one |
| `similar_app_ids` | array | detail | App IDs of the similar apps shown on the listing |
| `permission_groups` | array | detail | Permission groups the app asks for |
| `top_chart_label` | string or null | detail | Top chart the app appears in, as shown on the listing |
| `top_chart_rank` | string or null | detail | Rank in that chart, for example `#1` |
| `country` | string | both | Store country used |
| `language` | string | both | Language used |
| `search_query` | string or null | both | Keyword that returned the app; `null` for app IDs |
| `scraped_at` | string | both | UTC timestamp, ISO 8601 |

Developer contact fields are exactly what the listing shows publicly. Many listings show an email and a website, fewer show an address or a phone number. Dates are given as ISO timestamps from the source's own time values, so they do not change with the language setting; the `_text` fields keep the localised wording.

Fill rates, measured in one local test series in October 2026 (US store, English, plus one run in the German store; 30 app page rows and 57 search rows over several runs, some apps appear more than once): on the 30 app pages every field above was present except `version` and `android_version` (always empty), `video` (2 of 30), `developer_phone` (19 of 30), `developer_website` (27 of 30), `iap_price_range` (27 of 30), `recent_changes` (27 of 30), `content_rating_descriptors` (15 of 30) and `top_chart_label` / `top_chart_rank` (5 of 30). On the search results title, developer, category, installs, price, content rating, description and icon were present on every row, and `score` on all but 2 apps without a rating. These figures describe this test series, not a general rate.

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `searchQueries` | list of text | `["budget planner"]` when no keyword and no app is given | Keywords such as `habit tracker`. A comma or line separated text also works. |
| `appIds` | list of text | empty | Package names (`com.duolingo`) or app page URLs (`https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.duolingo`). Always returns the full record. |
| `country` | text | `us` | Two-letter store country: prices, ratings and availability follow it. |
| `language` | text | `en` | Language of titles, descriptions and labels, for example `de` or `pt-BR`. |
| `includeDetails` | boolean | `true` | Keyword results: open every app for the full record (billed as an app detail event). Off: search list fields only (billed as a search result event). |
| `maxResults` | integer | `50` | Maximum number of apps across all keywords and app IDs. `0` means no limit. The limit is shared equally between the entries; an unused share goes to the later ones. |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | integer | `0` | Maximum number of apps for each keyword and each app ID. `0` means no separate limit. |
| `proxyConfiguration` | object | `{"useApifyProxy": true}` | Proxy settings. The default works for most runs. |

Numbers may be given as text (`"25"`). An empty input `{}` runs a small sample search (`budget planner`, up to 10 apps, with details) and the run status says so. If the input cannot be read, the actor runs that same sample and writes a warning to the log. The same keyword or app given twice is processed once, and an app that several searches find is delivered once. A pasted Google Play search URL is read as its keyword. Values that are neither a package name nor a Play URL are skipped and counted in the status message.

### Example input

Search with full records:

```json
{
  "searchQueries": ["budget planner", "habit tracker"],
  "country": "us",
  "language": "en",
  "maxResults": 60
}
```

Look up apps:

```json
{
  "appIds": [
    "com.duolingo",
    "https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.spotify.music"
  ],
  "country": "de",
  "language": "de"
}
```

Search list fields only:

```json
{
  "searchQueries": ["chess"],
  "includeDetails": false,
  "maxResults": 30
}
```

## Pricing

Pay per result. The Pricing tab of this Actor shows the price of each event and the one-time start fee:

- `actor-start`: charged once per run, together with the first delivered app.
- `app-detail`: one per app delivered as a `detail` record. It is charged instead of, not on top of, `app-search-result`.
- `app-search-result`: one per app delivered as a `search` record.

You are charged only for apps that were delivered; a run that finds nothing costs nothing. If you set a maximum cost per run, the run stops at that limit and the status message says how many apps were delivered.

## Use with AI (MCP)

Add this actor as a tool in Claude or another MCP client:

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/google-play-scraper
```

Example prompts:
- "Find 30 budgeting apps in the US Play Store and list the developer email and website for each."
- "Get the rating, install band and last update date of com.duolingo and com.spotify.music."

## FAQ

**How many apps does one keyword return?** Up to 30: the first result page of the Google Play search. Further result pages are not read yet. For more volume, add keyword variants (for example `budget planner`, `budget app`, `expense tracker`) or use App IDs. When a keyword gives fewer apps than your limit allows, the status message says so.

**Why are `version` and `android_version` empty?** Google Play does not put them on the app page itself, so they are always `null`.

**Why is a developer email or address empty?** Only what the listing shows is returned. Not every developer publishes an email, website, address or phone number.

**Which store does `country` select?** The Google Play storefront of that country: prices, ratings, availability and the top chart label follow it. Use `language` for the text language.

**What is `installs_max`?** Google Play shows install bands such as `500,000,000+`. `installs_min` is the band start; `installs_max` is the start of the next band minus one, so it is a bound, not a measured number.

**Keyword results cost more with details. How do I keep the cost down?** Set `includeDetails` to `false` to get search list fields only, or use `maxResults` and a maximum cost per run.

**How do I find an app ID?** It is the `id=` part of the app page URL, for example `com.duolingo`. You can also paste the full URL.

## Limits

- Keyword searches read the first result page only (up to 30 apps per keyword).
- Top charts, category pages and developer pages are not supported yet.
- A search for a keyword in a small store can return few apps, or none; the run then ends normally with a message and no charge.
- Only public listing data is returned. Reviews are not included.

## Data protection

This actor returns only data that is publicly visible on the source pages. Results can include personal data, such as names, email addresses, phone numbers and addresses of individual developers or sole traders. You are responsible for using the data lawfully, including the GDPR/DSGVO, national data-protection laws and unfair-competition rules (for example UWG) for marketing and outreach.

## Support

Questions or problems? Open a ticket in the Issues tab on the actor page or email contact@nanoscrape.com.
